title: Schedule II opioid adverse-risk information and opioid-antagonist offer
rule_summary: When a pharmacist dispenses an opioid contained in Schedule II, Massachusetts law requires the pharmacist to inform the patient of the potential adverse risks of the prescription opioid and to offer to dispense an opioid antagonist to the patient and, where applicable, a designee; for a minor patient, the offer is made to the parent or guardian.
exam_relevance: Tests the pharmacist-specific duty triggered by dispensing a Schedule II opioid and distinguishes a mandatory risk discussion and antagonist offer from mandatory antagonist acceptance or prescriber-initiated antagonist prescribing.
exceptions: Section 18D does not state an exception based on prior opioid experience, possession of an opioid antagonist at home, or absence of a separate antagonist prescription from the opioid prescriber.
common_confusions: Treating the required offer as a requirement that the patient accept or purchase an opioid antagonist.
Conditioning the pharmacist duty on the prescriber having separately ordered an opioid antagonist.
Applying the duty to every controlled substance rather than to an opioid contained in Schedule II.
verification_notes: Current M.G.L. c.94C §18D checked on the Massachusetts Legislature and Mass.gov official law pages on 2026-08-14; section added by St. 2024, c.140, §109 and effective July 1, 2024.
